| stats count as id | eval id="11-22",

Let's take one range at a time to start with.,1,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1

| stats count as id | eval id="11-22" | rex field=id "(?\d+)-(?\d+)",

We need to enumerate each ID in the range. Let's start by getting the boundaries.,2,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1

| stats count as id | eval id="11-22" | rex field=id "(?\d+)-(?\d+)" | eval id=mvrange(min, max +1),"

We can use mvrange to enumerate the IDs.
Warning: if mvrange is asked to generate more than 10,000 values, it will only give the first 10,000 values with no error message.",3,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1

| stats count as id | eval id="11-22" | rex field=id "(?\d+)-(?\d+)" | eval id=mvrange(min, max +1) | fields id | mvexpand id,"

mvexpand will give us one event per ID, which sets us up to assess them in turn.",4,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1

| stats count as id | eval id="11-22" | rex field=id "(?\d+)-(?\d+)" | eval id=mvrange(min, max +1) | fields id | mvexpand id | regex id="^(.+)\1$","

The simplest way to identify IDs made of a repeated set of digits is to use a regular expression.
^ and $ anchor the pattern at the start and end of the ID.
The . means (almost) any character and + means ""1 or more"" of it.
The () brackets are defining a capturing group.
\1 is referring to whatever the content of the first capturing group is.",5,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1

| stats count as id | eval id="11-22" | rex field=id "(?\d+)-(?\d+)" | eval id=mvrange(min, max +1) | fields id | mvexpand id | eval len=len(id) | where len % 2 == 0 | eval width=len/2,"

Let's explore an alternative to regular expressions.
First we establish how big the chunks we need to look at, and we exclude IDs with an odd number of digits.",6,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1

| stats count as id | eval id="11-22" | rex field=id "(?\d+)-(?\d+)" | eval id=mvrange(min, max +1) | fields id | mvexpand id | eval len=len(id) | where len % 2 == 0 | eval width=len/2 | eval first_half = substr(id,1,len/2) | eval second_half= substr(id,len/2 + 1, len/2),"

Substr allows us to extract each half of the ID.
Warning: unlike some other eval functions (such as mvindex) substr use a one-based index.",7,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1

| stats count as id | eval id="11-22" | rex field=id "(?\d+)-(?\d+)" | eval id=mvrange(min, max +1) | fields id | mvexpand id | eval len=len(id) | where len % 2 == 0 | eval width=len/2 | eval first_half = substr(id,1,len/2) | eval second_half= substr(id,len/2 + 1, len/2) | where first_half==second_half | table id,

We keep the IDs where both halves are the same.,8,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1

| stats count as id | eval id="11-22" | rex field=id "(?\d+)-(?\d+)" | eval id=mvrange(min, max +1) | fields id | mvexpand id | regex id="^(.+)\1$",

We prefer using a regular expression.,9,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1

column1: No errors, but this gives the wrong solution because mvexpand silently maxes out at 10,000 values (no error message!).
We can fix this by developing a scalable version of mvrange. Launch the scalable mvrange lesson",12,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1 - full scale

| inputlookup adventofcode2025day2.csv | rex field=id "(?\d+)-(?\d+)" | `super_mvrange(id, min, max +1)` | fields id | mvexpand id | regex id="^(.+)\1$" | stats sum(id) as total,"

We have made mvexpand scalable, but now it's mvexpand that runs out of memory (notice the yellow triangle ⚠️).
Can we get replace mvexpand with something else?",13,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1 - full scale

| inputlookup adventofcode2025day2.csv | rex field=id "(?\d+)-(?\d+)" | `super_mvrange(id, min, max +1)` | fields id | stats count by id | regex id="^(.+)\1$" | stats sum(id) as total,"

A stats command is often a good replacement for mvexpand and it is much much more memory efficient.
The correct answer for this particular puzzle data is 43952536386.
But can you think of another way?",14,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1 - full scale

| inputlookup adventofcode2025day2.csv | rex field=id "(?\d+)-(?\d+)" | `super_mvrange(id, min, max +1)` | fields id | eval id=mvmap( id, if( match( id, "^(.+)\1$"), id, null() ) ) | stats sum(id) as total,"

How about that?
In this approach we keep id as a multivalue field and we filter it in-situ.
The correct answer for this particular puzzle data is (still) 43952536386.
The mvfilter is useful for basic filtering but for this kind of situation, a clever use of mvmap is what's needed.",15,AdventOfCode25 Day 2<-O->part 1 - full scale
